evidence.detail: The abstract base stores an interval and last-run timestamp; its final execution path calls the subclass hook only when the interval is zero or the elapsed wall-clock time reaches that interval, then updates last-run time.
The class statically owns and registers three int-keyed registries for its concrete interface-task subclasses and exposes one reset that clears every registry.

Exact-v308 consumers bind concrete subclasses to interface/widget ids for Event Activity refresh, Event Brawl status updates and hotspot hover tasks, fixing the abstraction as timed interface work rather than a generic scheduler.

evidence.detail: The class owns a Trove int-to-List map of TimedInterfaceTask instances; registration lazily creates the list for an integer key and appends the task.
Dispatch by integer key iterates the corresponding task list and invokes the TimedInterfaceTask interval-gated execution path for every registered task.

Concrete registrations use live interface/widget ids such as 30072, 40087 and 62150-62156, while rendering/input paths dispatch by the active RSInterface id, fixing the key domain to interface/widget identities.
